slots.hypothesis: The core telescopes to (last-30-min shares minus first-30-min shares)/211. It is a slow intraday volume-timing profile, sign -1 (long open-heavy names). No outer piece that only rescales by a daily scalar: in rank terms C/V has rho about 0.85 with C, so those go to R. There are 13 seeds over four kinds of outer piece. (1) Scale-free persistence: cross_ema(sign C, 10) and the 20-day mean/std ratio. (2) Tilt that is unusual for the stock's own history: cross_zscore, cross_delta, ts_regres and cross_regbeta of C on daily volume, and C times the volume z-score. (3) Tilt read through price: C times the sign of the day's return and its 20-day mean, cross_corr with the daily return, C times the overnight gap, and a rank-centred product with the last-30-min return (Llorente et al. 2001; Boyarchenko et al. 2020). (4) Auction separated from continuous trading: cs_regres of C on the 5-minute tilt (Givry 2019; Han et al. 2022).

Intraday volume-price coupling: whether volume arrives with rises or falls, and how hard price moves at volume bursts. This is a dimension the unsigned endpoint-timing head ignores. Llorente et al. 2001: informed volume continues and liquidity volume reverses. Barber-Odean 2008: attention bursts bring retail buying and later underperformance. The 13 seeds are all scale-free: day_corr of Ret or Close with Volume; Ret against in_delta(Volume,1); day_signed_ratio (net buying pressure); volume-weighted minus equal-weighted minute return; lead/lag correlations of volume and price; and burst minutes picked by in_zscore_rolling(Volume,30), measured by mean return and by volatility relative to the day. The last two seeds are 20-day means of day_corr(Close,Volume) and of day_signed_ratio.
